Description

CGRP, released with substance P from peptidergic afferents, acts on a receptor made of the calcitonin receptor-like receptor and RAMP1. The receptor couples to Gs and raises cAMP. In the dorsal horn it lies mainly on presynaptic terminals, where it can modulate transmitter release. In OA models CGRP sensitises joint nociceptors to mechanical stimuli.

Colour

Proteins and metabolites are coloured by their contribution to pain: red for those that raise it (they excite or sensitise nociceptive neurons, or drive the inflammation that does), blue for those that relieve it, and olive for the shared signalling machinery (G proteins, RGS, adenylate cyclase, phospholipases, kinases, adaptors, second messengers, ions and nucleotides), whose effect is set by the receptor upstream. Metabolites take a lighter shade of the same colour. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white. Each molecule is coloured by its role in this block, so the same molecule can be red in one block and blue in another.

CGRP and its receptor (CALCRL with RAMP1) are red as transmitters of nociceptive signals. On immune cells CGRP acts the other way: it inhibits the production of TNF by macrophages through cAMP (Feng 1997). Pain is the endpoint of this map, so the colour follows the action on the neuron.
